summary: Registered a competing-cause control for the now-asserted snapshot-boundary loop. The earlier update (update-10.json) recorded the measured interpretation of the sealed-partition receipt CheckRun f66fa4e4e0514f7e95b7788032144a30 (exit 0, tests_passed): with the partition actually sealing {leader, partner} from the other three peers, the legal five-node history reaches the precondition through real producers (divergent_prefix index 1: partitioned_leader_last_index 7, partner_last_index 7, partner_store 1..7), the successor snapshots inside the partner's stale suffix with its store fully compacted (index 2: snapshot_index 4, successor_store 0/0), and after the heal the partner installs the same snapshot 668 times in ~1.5 s (index 9: restores_before 0, restores_early 658, restores_late 668) while its applied index stays pinned at 4 and its advertised last index stays 7 — conclusion violated, defect_claim asserted, with the mechanism traced to the nextIndex rewind landing on the snapshot boundary, ErrLogNotFound from the compacted leader log, SEND_SNAP and re-installation of the same snapshot. This update adds the control: the same harness now runs the identical history twice, differing only in how much log the successor retains when it snapshots. Locally, TrailingLogs=0 gives restores_early 724 / restores_late 734 with partner_applied_index 4 and partner_last_index 7, while TrailingLogs=3 gives restores 0 with partner_applied_index 4 and partner_last_index 4 — the same history converges by ordinary AppendEntries with no snapshot at all, isolating leader compaction past the index needed to rebuild the request as the load-bearing condition. The new investigation @q-compaction-cause and its two-case experiment are registered so the controller retains that receipt; the interpretation stays conclusion=unresolved / defect_claim=unresolved in this batch (it cannot link a receipt to a fixed experiment) and records the counterevidence and the unsampled default-TrailingLogs case. Structural validation returned valid=true.
